context:
## Why AMBER and not RED

The computed colour this run was **RED**, on A3 — three asks past drop-dead. John Costa overrode it to AMBER on Jul 22 on the grounds that CORZA-159 has a workaround in place. The override expires Jul 29 and is shown with the computed colour beside it, always: "machine says red, John says amber, because Y" is the most useful sentence a weekly risk read produces, and hiding either half breaks it.

## The honest dynamic range

Two of the three RED conditions cannot fire:

- **R1** needs a per-ask `Blocking?` marker. No source carries one — not the register, not Jira. It is structurally untestable, not merely unmet this week.
- **R2** tests `launch.required > launch.actual`. `corza-progress` refuses to publish that pair, in its own words: *"extrapolating a launch rate from a team mid-ramp is exactly the forecast the next section refuses."* This banner must not resolve that by deriving the pace itself — deriving nothing is the whole basis of its independence.

So RED is reachable only through R3. Resolving either is an ADR-shaped decision, not a template edit.

## Trend

Compared against Jul 29, the last run on a previous calendar day — never simply the previous commit, because a re-run an hour later is a correction rather than a day of progress.

## Ask me about

Whether the override should be renewed on Jul 29 or allowed to lapse to the computed colour; what it would take to give R1 a real input; and whether rule-set B should shrink to the conditions that can actually fire.
